title: How to get psychology research published before you graduate

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有个好消息要宣布。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many program is now open for enrollment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特（Sophie Foote）的“一对多”项目现在开放报名了。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可规模化的产品，比如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己在2022年完成了这个项目，从那以后，我也一直在支持两届心理学家完成他们的旅程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的专属联盟链接加入，你将获得苏菲的额外福利以及我提供的专属支持套餐，无需额外付费。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalized guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.

sentences.en: Enrollment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名将于11月16日星期一晚上10点截止。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的福利。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时都在。

sentences.en: Coming up in today's episode, I am talking to Matthew, who is an early career psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 在今天的节目中，我将与马修（Matthew）对话，他是一名初入职场的心理学新手。

sentences.en: He is in the middle of his undergraduate psychology degree.
sentences.zh: 他目前正读本科心理学专业的中期。

sentences.en: And we are talking about research, how he has managed to get himself such robust, important research experience before he has even graduated.
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论研究，以及他是如何在甚至还没毕业的情况下，就设法积累到如此扎实、重要的研究经验的。

sentences.en: It is a brilliant episode.

sentences.en: And, you know, you learn along the way and maybe you will like particular areas.
sentences.zh: 也许你不会。

sentences.en: Maybe you won't.
sentences.zh: 但，你知道的，保留那些对你行之有效的领域，并从那些不太顺利的事情中吸取教训。

sentences.en: But it's, you know, keeping the things that work well for you and learning from the bits that don't go so well.
sentences.zh: 在英国，我认为在临床神经心理学方面，你需要先完成临床心理学，然后攻读神经心理学硕士学位。

sentences.en: In the UK, I think in terms of clinical neuropsychology, you do your clinical psychology and then do a master's in neuropsychology.
sentences.zh: 你的本科学位是否符合英国心理学会（British Psychological Society）的认可标准，以便能够进入英国的博士项目？

sentences.en: Does your undergraduate confer the British Psychological Society kind of mark of approval in order to get onto UK doctorates?
sentences.zh: 还是说，因为你在爱尔兰，情况会有些不同？

sentences.en: Or is it is it a little bit different with you being in Ireland?
sentences.zh: 还是说，你在爱尔兰的情况会有点不一样？

sentences.en: As far as I know, I think so, because I know the HSE, like the health services here for assistant psychologist roles.
sentences.zh: 就我所知，我觉得是这样的，因为我了解HSE，比如这里针对助理心理学家职位的健康服务部门。

sentences.en: They look for like degrees that are accredited by the PSI, the Irish Psychological Society or the British British one.
sentences.zh: 他们寻找的是通过PSI（爱尔兰心理学会）或英国心理学会认证的学位。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: OK, lovely.
sentences.zh: 好的，太棒了。

sentences.en: So I guess that means hopefully you've got options available for you to train in Ireland or maybe in the UK as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜这意味着希望你能在爱尔兰或英国也有培训的选择。

sentences.en: Yeah, that would be great.
sentences.zh: 对，那太好了。

sentences.en: Yeah, hopefully.
sentences.zh: 对，希望如此。

sentences.en: So you mentioned your research paper there.
sentences.zh: 那么你刚才提到了你的研究论文。

sentences.en: Could you tell us a little bit about what you've been up to?
sentences.zh: 能给我们讲讲你一直在做什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: So last year they sent out a call for kind of scholarships during the summer research internships.
sentences.zh: 所以去年他们发出了一个关于暑期研究实习奖学金的征集通知。

sentences.en: And I sent an email to one of my lecturers, Dr. Tom Burke.
sentences.zh: 然后我给我的讲师之一，汤姆·伯克（Tom Burke）博士发了一封邮件。

sentences.en: He's a clinical neuropsychologist in the hospital in Galway here.
sentences.zh: 他是这里戈尔韦医院的一名临床神经心理学家。

sentences.en: And I told him I had an interest in schizophrenia and kind of like social cognition and personality disorders and different stuff like that.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他我对精神分裂症、社会认知、人格障碍以及诸如此类不同的东西很感兴趣。

sentences.en: So he recommended to apply for a neuroscience, the Galway neuroscience scholarship.
sentences.zh: 于是他建议我申请一个神经科学奖学金，即戈尔韦神经科学奖学金。

sentences.en: So he kind of told me like there's a data set they've already collected.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我他们已经收集好了一组数据集。

sentences.en: They've been working on called Irelate,
sentences.zh: 他们一直在进行一个名为Irelate的项目，

sentences.en: a very big data set of people living with schizophrenia and kind of different social cognition tests and childhood trauma and genetics as well.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于精神分裂症患者的大型数据集，其中包含各种社会认知测试、童年创伤以及遗传学等方面的内容。

sentences.en: So, yeah, he said I could work on that data set and maybe to pick a white matter tract.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，他说我可以处理那个数据集，或者挑选一个白质纤维束。

sentences.en: So I did some research and came up with the unsnit vesiculus.
sentences.zh: 于是我做了一些研究，选中了钩束（uncinate fasciculus）。

sentences.en: It's like a frontal white matter tract.
sentences.zh: 它就像是一个额叶白质纤维束。

sentences.en: And he was like unbelievably helpful, like super supportive.
sentences.zh: 他真的非常乐于助人，超级支持我。

sentences.en: I definitely wouldn't have been able to do any of it without his guidance.
sentences.zh: 如果没有他的指导，我绝对不可能完成这一切。

sentences.en: So he guided me along and we came up with an idea for the relationship between emotion recognition.
sentences.zh: 因此他在一旁指导我，我们共同构思了一个关于情绪识别关系的想法。

sentences.en: Like, I suppose, a facet of social cog is emotion recognition, the unsnit and childhood trauma.
sentences.zh: 我想，社会认知的一个方面就是情绪识别、钩束以及童年创伤。

sentences.en: So we kind of looked at the relationship between those three and kind of whether physical neglect in childhood kind of mediated the relationship between social cognition and the development of the unsnit vesiculus in the brain.
sentences.zh: 所以我们探讨了这三者之间的关系，以及童年时期的身体忽视是否在社会认知与大脑中钩束发育之间的关系中起到了中介作用。

sentences.en: With the theory being that the tract is somehow linked and important to whether someone does or doesn't develop schizophrenia, is that where it's rooted in?
sentences.zh: 其理论是，这个纤维束在某种程度上与一个人是否会患上精神分裂症息息相关，这是它的根源所在吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, sort of, sort of, kind of, maybe it might be to do with social cognition.
sentences.zh: 对，有点像，可以说是，可能跟社会认知有关。

sentences.en: And we're kind of thinking maybe childhood trauma affects the development of that white matter tract.
sentences.zh: 我们在想，也许童年创伤会影响那个白质纤维束的发育。

sentences.en: And then through affecting that, as the person grows older, their emotion recognition might be negatively affected.
sentences.zh: 然后通过影响它，随着人逐渐长大，他们的情绪识别能力可能会受到负面影响。

sentences.en: And then that could contribute to the development of schizophrenia that they might already be at risk for or other factors might be playing at risk.
sentences.zh: 这可能会导致精神分裂症的发作，而他们可能本身就已经存在这种风险，或者有其他风险因素在起作用。

sentences.en: But it was really interesting in the research looking at, I suppose, how emotion recognition can play into someone who might be experiencing psychosis or at risk.
sentences.zh: 但这项研究真的非常有趣，我想，它探讨了情绪识别如何影响那些可能正在经历精神精神病发作或面临风险的人。

sentences.en: They actually found that poor emotion recognition of neutral faces was predictive of transition to psychosis in people who are at risk.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上发现，对中性面孔的情绪识别能力差，可以预测高风险人群向精神病的转化。

sentences.en: So someone might be talking to someone in a social setting and then they're picking up maybe an angry face from someone who has a neutral expression.
sentences.zh: 所以，当某人在社交场合与人交谈时，他们可能会从一个表情中立的人脸上解读出愤怒的表情。

sentences.en: And maybe if that person already is at risk and maybe has maybe some delusional thinking or kind of paranoid thought styles that they might start thinking, oh,
sentences.zh: 也许如果这个人已经处于风险之中，并且可能有一些妄想思维或偏执的思考方式，他们就会开始想：

sentences.en: this person's angry at me and could cause a lot of distress then, I suppose.
sentences.zh: “这人对我很生气”，我想这会带来很大的痛苦。

sentences.en: Yeah, and that's got really useful utility for even for us working with people with psychosis, because actually when we were using our listening faces, they might look quite blank.
sentences.zh: 对，这对我们这些与精神病患者工作的人来说非常有用，因为实际上当我们使用倾听表情时，我们的脸可能看起来相当空白。

sentences.en: They might look quite neutral.
sentences.zh: 我们可能看起来非常中立。

sentences.en: And if that can be interpreted really like negatively or hostilely, is that a word?
sentences.zh: 如果这被非常负面地或充满敌意地解读——“敌意”这个词是这么用的吗？

sentences.en: Then that's problematic, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那就有问题了，对吧？

sentences.en: So I guess this is why I love research, because it teaches us so much about the person, about their experience of the world and, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我想这就是我热爱研究的原因，因为它教给我们太多关于一个人、关于他们对世界的体验，以及你知道的，

sentences.en: how to understand and make things less friction-y, you know, so that things work better all round and that people have a better experience of it.
sentences.zh: 如何去理解并减少摩擦，你知道的，让一切运转得更好，让人们有更好的体验。

sentences.en: You mentioned a data set there, but it wasn't one I'm familiar with.
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到一个数据集，但这不是我熟悉的一个。

sentences.en: Could you tell us what the data set is?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我们那是什么数据集吗？

sentences.en: How do you spell the data set that you mentioned?
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到的那个数据集怎么拼写？

sentences.en: So it's like a lowercase i and then the word relate.
sentences.zh: 它是小写的 i，后面跟上单词 relate。

sentences.en: So R-E-L-A-T-E.
sentences.zh: 也就是 R-E-L-A-T-E。

sentences.en: I'm not, you know, I don't fully understand the whole project.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说，你知道的，我完全理解整个项目。

sentences.en: It's a very big project, but it's ongoing.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常大的项目，而且还在进行中。

sentences.en: There's been a lot of papers published from it, and it did a big kind of neuroimaging on people living with schizophrenia and social cognition tests.
sentences.zh: 已经有很多关于它的论文发表了，它对精神分裂症患者和社交认知测试进行了大规模的神经成像。

sentences.en: You know, and kind of what my supervisor, Dr. Burke, said to me was, these people have given their time, you know, for us to collect this data.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我的导师伯克博士对我说过：这些人奉献了他们的时间，让我们能够收集这些数据。

sentences.en: So it's important that we kind of use it to the fullest that we can to, you know, benefit other people.
sentences.zh: 所以重要的是，我们要尽可能充分地利用它，去造福其他人。

sentences.en: So, yeah, there's actually a really interesting documentary about schizophrenia on R-E-L-A-T-E.
sentences.zh: 所以，有一个关于R-E-L-A-T-E精神分裂症的非常有趣的纪录片。

sentences.en: I'm not sure it's not on R-E-L-A-T-E now, but if you look it up online, it might come up.
sentences.zh: 我不确定它现在是不是还在R-E-L-A-T-E上，但如果你在网上搜一下，可能会搜到。

sentences.en: And there's lecturers from University of Galway and from the IRLA project and the lead of that project, Professor Gary O'Donoghue.
sentences.zh: 那里有来自戈尔韦大学的讲师、IRLATE项目的成员，还有该项目的负责人加里·奥多诺休（Gary O'Donoghue）教授。

sentences.en: And he talks about schizophrenia and about the project.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了精神分裂症和这个项目。

sentences.en: And, yeah, it's really fascinating if anyone's interested.
sentences.zh: 如果有人感兴趣的话，真的非常迷人。

sentences.en: Sounds great.
sentences.zh: 听起来很棒。

sentences.en: I can see why this has kind of evoked this interest in you.
sentences.zh: 我能看出为什么这会在你心中激起这样的兴趣。

sentences.en: And I guess what I really love is that you're learning so much at a stage of your career where actually usually we're probably quite limited just to textbooks.
sentences.zh: 我想我真正喜欢的是，在你职业生涯的这个阶段，你学到了这么多东西，而通常我们可能只限于课本。

sentences.en: But you're seeing that real world applications and real world research for this.
sentences.zh: 但你看到了这背后的现实应用和现实世界的研究。

sentences.en: And I think that lights you up, you know, and but kudos to you as well, Matthew, because you're clearly the kind of guy that reaches out and asks for opportunities,
sentences.zh: 我认为这让你焕发光彩，你知道的，不过也要向你致敬，马修（Matthew），因为你显然是那种会主动出击、争取机会的人，

sentences.en: you know, like you did with coming on the podcast and like you did with even approaching the professor at Galway Uni.
sentences.zh: 就像你上这个播客一样，就像你主动联系戈尔韦大学的教授一样。

sentences.en: You know, you have the idea and you give yourself permission to to ask and to explore.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你有了想法，然后允许自己去询问和探索。

sentences.en: And, you know, the worst they can ever do is say no, but you never know where it might lead.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们最多也只能说不，但你永远不知道这会通向哪里。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think something I've learned the last few years is that, you know, it's always worth taking chances.
sentences.zh: 是的，过去几年我学到的一点是，抓住机会总是值得的。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of the a lot of the good things that have happened over the past few years is because other people get me chances.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，过去几年发生的好多好多事情，都是因为其他人给了我机会。

sentences.en: And I kind of give myself a chance in a lot of situations.
sentences.zh: 而且在很多情况下，我也给了自己一个机会。

sentences.en: Just like earlier this year, I started I used to do boxing when I was younger.
sentences.zh: 就像今年早些时候我开始的——我小时候练过拳击。

sentences.en: I kind of lost it for a while.
sentences.zh: 我有一段时间荒废了。

sentences.en: So I went back.
sentences.zh: 所以我又回去了。

sentences.en: I started MMA and that was just like, you know, obviously I was super nervous beforehand,
sentences.zh: 我开始练综合格斗（MMA），当时的感觉就是，你知道的，虽然我事先超级紧张，

sentences.en: but it was just something like throwing myself in there and and challenging myself with something new and kind of giving giving myself a chance to,
sentences.zh: 但这就好把自己投身其中，用新鲜事物挑战自己，给自己一个机会去——

sentences.en: I guess, to take a chance and see what happens.
sentences.zh: 我想，去抓住机会，看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: And it's honestly been one of the best decisions in my life.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这是我一生中做出的最好决定之一。

sentences.en: You know, just it's been so important for connecting myself back with my body while I'm while I'm kind of psychology can get very up here.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这对于重新建立我和身体的联系非常重要，而在心理学领域，思维往往会变得很高深。

sentences.en: So it's kind of an important balance for me to to have both.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，两兼顾是一个很重要的平衡。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Exercise is only something I've really come to a latter stage of my current life.
sentences.zh: 运动是我到了当前人生的晚期阶段才真正开始接触的事情。

sentences.en: I was a latter life, but I'm only 42.
sentences.zh: 我说的是人生后半段，其实我才42岁。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Like it just wasn't something that was around for me, but I really, really enjoy it now.
sentences.zh: 这以前真不是我生活中的一部分，但我现在真的很喜欢它。

sentences.en: And I like you say, it helps me to to balance myself kind of.
sentences.zh: 就像你说的，它帮我达到了一种平衡。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Body and mind.
sentences.zh: 身心合一。

sentences.en: So with your, you know, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 所以你的，完全没错。

sentences.en: What you said is right that the professor had said we've got a duty of care, really,
sentences.zh: 你说的很对，教授曾说过，我们确实有一份关怀责任，

sentences.en: to to do everything we can with this research, with these, you know, this data that the people have given so freely of their time to create.
sentences.zh: 要尽我们所能利用这份研究，利用人们如此慷慨奉献时间所创造的数据。

sentences.en: So what did you do with it?
sentences.zh: 那你用它做了什么？

sentences.en: What happened next?
sentences.zh: 接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we had, I think, just about 105, well, 58 participants.
sentences.zh: 我们大概有105个，嗯，58个参与者。

sentences.en: And then, I'm not sure, 116, whatever double that is, I had to basically use a software.
sentences.zh: 然后，我不确定，116个，或者两倍那个数字，我基本上得使用一个软件。

sentences.en: It's a diffusion, diffusion tensor imaging software.
sentences.zh: 这是一个弥散张量成像（DTI）软件。

sentences.en: So we had all the MRI scans and then they were transferred to, I think, a DTI file.
sentences.zh: 所以我们拥有所有的磁共振成像（MRI）扫描结果，然后它们被转换成，我想是一个DTI文件。

sentences.en: And then I used that program.
sentences.zh: 然后我就用了那个程序。

sentences.en: It was really fascinating.
sentences.zh: 真的非常神奇。

sentences.en: It was a bit mind blown at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时觉得有点脑洞大开。

sentences.en: I could basically see their brain scan in kind of 3D.
sentences.zh: 我基本上可以以3D的形式看到他们的脑部扫描。

sentences.en: And part of the internship was to learn how to segment a tract.
sentences.zh: 实习的一部分就是学习如何分割一个纤维束。

sentences.en: So to basically get rid of all the other white matter tracts and single out on this specific one.
sentences.zh: 也就是基本上清除所有其他的白质纤维束，单挑出这一个特定的纤维束。

sentences.en: And then we used a measure called fractional anisotrophy.
sentences.zh: 然后我们使用了一个名为“部分各向异性”（fractional anisotropy）的测量指标。

sentences.en: So kind of a measure of the water diffusion in the tract and how the integrity of the tract.
sentences.zh: 这可以用来衡量纤维束中的水分子弥散情况以及纤维束的完整性。

sentences.en: So whether those water molecules are really, like, densely packed together or kind of sparsed out.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些水分子是紧密地挤在一起，还是比较稀疏。

sentences.en: And that can kind of, I suppose, by looking at other research, that can give us an indication of how well kind of functioning it is.
sentences.zh: 我想，通过参考其他研究，这可以让我们了解它的功能运作得有多好。

sentences.en: So, like, my supervisor gave a really good analogy of it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的导师给了一个非常好的类比。

sentences.en: It's kind of like a road from one place to another.
sentences.zh: 它就像是从一个地方到另一个地方的道路。

sentences.en: And the white matter tract is, like, the road sending the information.
sentences.zh: 而白质纤维束就像是发送信息的道路。

sentences.en: And then if there's, like, potholes on that road, it can kind of information can get a bit damaged on the way.
sentences.zh: 如果在路上有类似“路坑”的东西，信息在传输途中可能会有点受损。

sentences.en: So basically, I went through just over 100 left and right on the left and right sides of the brain.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我查看了大脑左右两侧刚刚超过100个样本。

sentences.en: So the bilateral internets segmented all of those.
sentences.zh: 所以双侧的钩束全都被我分割出来了。

sentences.en: And we ran the statistics on the FAA values.
sentences.zh: 然后我们对FA值进行了统计分析。

sentences.en: And then we had pre-collected social cognition tests data and childhood trauma.
sentences.zh: 接着我们有预先收集的社交认知测试数据和童年创伤数据。

sentences.en: So we just kind of did some, like, mediation analysis and correlations and kind of seeing what was coming out of those.
sentences.zh: 所以我们就做了一些中介分析和相关性分析，看看能得出什么结果。

sentences.en: And, yeah.
sentences.zh: 然后，就这样。

sentences.en: Absolutely incredible.
sentences.zh: 简直不可思议。

sentences.en: And hearing you speak, like, even I don't know what this stuff is.
sentences.zh: 听你说话，甚至连我都不知道这些东西是什么。

sentences.en: It's, like, it's amazing, like, even that you get to know this stuff and you get to be so competent and, you know,
sentences.zh: 这太惊人了，你竟然能了解这些，而且能对你所谈论和理解的内容表现得如此胜任、

sentences.en: capable at what you're talking about and what you're understanding.
sentences.zh: 专业和能力出众。

sentences.en: This is massively important.
sentences.zh: 这极其重要。

sentences.en: And, you know, it sounds like you, you know, just really found a really wonderful opportunity where you've been able to help, you know, a research process.
sentences.zh: 而且，听起来你确实找到了一个绝佳的机会，能够协助推进一项研究进程。

sentences.en: But you've also learned so much.
sentences.zh: 但你也学到了很多东西。

sentences.en: And, you know, that will be useful for you in all of your areas of your career in the future.
sentences.zh: 并且，这将在你未来职业生涯的各个领域对你大有裨益。

sentences.en: You know, you'll have this understanding about the way that the brain works and what might stop it from working.
sentences.zh: 你将对大脑的工作方式以及是什么阻止它正常工作有这种理解。

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so, you know, absolutely.
